# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

# Review find-related skill

## Problem statement

The find-related skill was reported as slow and verbose (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9). This task reviews whether the v3 improvements have adequately addressed these concerns and whether further improvements are warranted.

## Existing state

The find-related skill underwent a major v3 overhaul (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9) that addressed two root causes:

**Speed**: v2 had a per-keyword subprocess fan-out problem (523 keywords → 523 `wl search` spawns at ~0.5s each → ≥240s timeout). v3 caps worklog search to the top 8 frequency-ranked keywords (one subprocess each), reducing search from 523 spawns to 8 (~4s). The feedback loop (where the automated report's tokens fed back into keyword extraction, growing from 14 → 82 → 523) was closed by stripping the report section before keyword extraction.

**Verbosity**: v2's report included raw keyword lists (58% of report bloat) and scanned `.worklog/` (83% of scanned files, including stale worktree clones and the skill's own sidecar report). v3 caps matched keywords per file at 5 with a `(+N more)` marker, excludes `.worklog` from repo scans, and uses deterministic section boundaries for idempotency.

**Measured improvements**:
- Wall-clock: ≥240s (timeout) → ~3s
- Subprocesses: 523 → 8
- Repo scan files: 2,188 → 362 (83% reduction)
- Keywords: 523 (unbounded) → 8 (capped at MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS)
- Report duplicates on re-run: stacked `###` blocks → single atomic replacement

## Assessment

The v3 changes directly address the original concerns about speed and verbosity. The skill now:
- Runs in ~1-3s for typical work items
- Produces compact, deterministic reports
- Is idempotent across re-runs
- Excludes non-authoritative directories from scans

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm the v3 improvements have been merged and deployed
- [ ] Verify the skill runs in <5s on representative work items
- [ ] Verify reports are compact and useful (no verbose keyword dumps)
- [ ] Verify idempotency (re-runs produce identical output)
- [ ] Document any remaining issues or further improvement opportunities

## Constraints

- Review should be evidence-driven (measure current performance)
- Any further improvements should be tracked as separate work items
- Do not re-implement v3 changes already applied

## Key files (review targets)

- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — Skill documentation (v3 changes documented)
- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — Implementation
- `docs/dev/find-related-v3-analysis.md` — Performance analysis with before/after metrics
- `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9.md` — Current full report output

## Related work

- SA-0MS3CIU1400272WT — Migrate skill/find-related to use StatusLifecycle
- SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH — Fix legacy skill/ path refs introduced by StatusLifecycle migration
- SA-0MS7FO6TO001ZBF0 — Fix pre-existing test failures: test_audit_skill_doc.py

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: The v3 changes have been fully merged. Verify via commit history.
- **Risk**: The work item was created before v3 was implemented; the assessment may be retrospective.
- **Risk**: "Value of content returned" is subjective — define what "value" means (relevance, actionability, completeness).
- **Scope creep**: This is a review, not an implementation. Further improvements should be separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'slow' mean in this context?" — Answer (work item description): Unspecified threshold. Evidence: v3 analysis shows 240s timeout → ~3s; current run: ~1s. Assessed as resolved.
- Q: "What does 'verbose' mean in this context?" — Answer (work item description): Unspecified. Evidence: v3 caps keyword lists at 5 per file with `(+N more)`; report sections use `MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS=3` and `MAX_REPO_FILE_RESULTS=3`. Assessed as resolved.
- Q: "Is there a specific work item to test against?" — Answer: The work item itself (SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9) was used as a test case in the v3 analysis. Current run confirms ~1s execution.

# Ralph model resolution bug: Local Proxy fallback incorrectly returns user prompt as response

## Problem Statement

When Ralph is run with `--model-source remote`, the model resolution logic fails to select the configured remote model (e.g., `opencode-go/qwen3.6-plus`) and instead falls back to `Local Proxy/qwen3`. When the Local Proxy endpoint is unavailable, Pi echoes the **user's skill prompt** back as the assistant's response, leading Ralph to report false successes with no actual model inference — wasting compute and never completing work items.

## Users

- **AI Agent Operators** — Users running Ralph to orchestrate implement→audit loops across projects.
- **Developer Experience** — Anyone relying on Ralph automation to reliably drive work items to completion.

### User Stories

- As an operator, I want Ralph to use the correct model when I specify `--model-source remote`, so that my configured remote models are actually used.
- As an operator, I want Ralph to detect when Pi returns echoed input instead of a real model response, so that silent failures are caught and reported.
- As a maintainer, I want the Pi JSON output parser to never extract user-message content as assistant responses, so that downstream processing is not corrupted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Model resolution correctness**: When `--model-source remote` is specified, Ralph must select the configured remote model for each phase (e.g., `opencode-go/qwen3.6-plus` for implementation, `opencode-go/kimi-k2.5` for audit) — not fall back to `Local Proxy/qwen3` or any other local model.

2. **User message filtering**: The `_parse_pi_json_line()` function must never extract content from `role=user` messages as assistant response text. Only `role=assistant` messages should contribute to the response text.

3. **Failure detection on empty/no-response**: When Pi returns no valid assistant response (e.g., empty assistant content, all errors/timeouts), Ralph must fail the attempt with a clear error rather than reporting success with echoed user content.

4. **No regression in existing behavior**: All existing Ralph tests must continue to pass. Local model flows (`--model-source local`) must behave identically to before the fix.

5. **Testing and validation**: Unit tests must be added covering:
   - Model resolution returns correct model for each `model_source` value
   - `_parse_pi_json_line()` correctly filters user-message content
   - Failure detection on empty/error Pi responses
   - The fix works correctly when Local Proxy endpoint is available

6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Backward compatibility: Existing `.ralph.json` configurations must continue to work.
- No new external dependencies should be required.
- The fix must not introduce breaking changes to the Ralph loop interface (CLI flags, config schema, output format).
- The default model source (`remote`) must continue to work for users who don't specify `--model-source`.

## Existing State

### Model Resolution Chain (current behavior)

1. User specifies: `--model-source remote`
2. Asset config (`skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json`) specifies:
   - remote.implementation: `opencode-go/qwen3.6-plus`
   - remote.audit: `opencode-go/kimi-k2.5`
   - local.implementation: `Qwen 32B`
3. Expected model: `opencode-go/qwen3.6-plus` (for implementation)
4. **Actual model used: `Local Proxy/qwen3`** — WRONG

### The False Success Bug

When `Local Proxy/qwen3` endpoint is down (192.168.0.199:8000 times out):

1. Pi invokes `/skill:audit <work-item-id>`
2. Pi loads the audit skill content (~9-10KB) as the USER message
3. Local Proxy times out after retries
4. Pi returns JSON stream with:
   - `message_start`/`message_end` events containing the USER message (role=user)
   - Empty assistant messages (role=assistant, content=[])
   - `agent_end` with messages list where last assistant has empty content
5. **BUG**: Ralph's `_parse_pi_json_line()` or `_extract_text_from_json_output()` incorrectly extracts the **user message content** as response text

### Related Unmerged Work

A related fix exists on branch `wl-SA-0MPKAZUWF0046EQJ-input-echo-detection` (commit `f13c4d5`) addressing input echo detection, but this branch has **not been merged** into `main`. This current work item should verify whether that fix is still relevant, supersedes it, or needs to be integrated.

## Desired Change

1. **Fix model resolution**: Debug and fix `_resolve_model_for_phase()` to correctly select remote models when `--model-source remote` is specified. Verify that config loading order, symlink resolution, and argument parsing are not interfering.

2. **Fix message extraction in `_parse_pi_json_line()`**: Add an explicit check to never extract from `role=user` messages. Only extract from `role=assistant` messages.

3. **Add failure detection**: Detect when all Pi responses are errors/timeouts with no valid assistant content and raise a clear error instead of reporting success.

4. **Build/test/commit**: Follow the mandatory build → test → commit order throughout.

## Related Work

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MPKAZUWF0046EQJ** — "Ralph: Silent failure when Pi echoes input instead of executing" (completed, not merged): Direct predecessor addressing the same input echo problem. Branch `wl-SA-0MPKAZUWF0046EQJ-input-echo-detection` exists with an implementation but was never merged into main. This current work item may supersede or incorporate that fix. The earlier item detected when Pi echoes input back, but this current bug goes deeper — it also addresses _why_ the wrong model is selected, which causes the Local Proxy fallback in the first place.
- **SA-0MPFD4RMU005NF9C** — "Ralph: Investigate missing user-facing text in Pi/LLM responses (no_text_extracted)" (completed): Investigated a case where Pi returns structurally valid JSON but no user-facing text. Shares the same `_parse_pi_json_line()` code path. The current bug is related but distinct — here text IS extracted, but from the wrong source (user message instead of assistant message).
- **SA-0MPKCSFSF008NTAH** — "Ralph Pi stream stalls on remote models" (completed): Made Pi stream timeout configurable per model source (60s local / 300s remote). Relevant context because this work item also touches the same remote-model execution path, and understanding the timeout behavior is important for debugging model failures.
- **SA-0MPFD4SG7008VVH6** — "Ralph: Support structured-only Pi responses (parse remediation actions from JSON)" (completed): Implemented structured response parsing for Pi JSON output. Shares the same streaming parser path where the false success bug occurs.
- **SA-0MPDVN9H6000HGMY** — "Update ralph skill to use optimal models per step" (completed): Updated per-phase model routing configuration in `.ralph.json`. Directly relevant because the model resolution bug means the per-phase config is not being correctly applied.
- **SA-0MPKYR7SS000CO2J** — "Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports" (open, intake_complete): Open item about Ralph status output consistency. Loosely related as a separate Ralph observability issue.

### Key Files

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — `_resolve_model_for_phase()` (model resolution), `_parse_pi_json_line()` (JSON event parsing), `_extract_text_from_json_output()` (text extraction)
- `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` — Default model configuration per source and phase
- `skill/ralph/tests/` — Test files for coverage
- `docs/ralph.md` — Ralph documentation
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — Skill definition
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` — Pi provider configuration (Local Proxy endpoint)

### Related Docs

- `docs/ralph.md` — Ralph orchestration loop documentation
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — Ralph skill definition with CLI flags and usage

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: The description identifies two distinct bugs (model resolution + false success). Additional issues may be discovered during debugging. **Mitigation**: Record any new issues as separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding scope.
- **Model resolution root cause unknown**: The exact reason Local Proxy/qwen3 is selected over the remote model is not yet confirmed — could be config loading order, symlink issues, stale bytecode, or argument parsing edge case.
- **Regression risk**: Changes to `_parse_pi_json_line()` or `_resolve_model_for_phase()` could affect other code paths that depend on these functions.
- **Duplicate/unmerged work**: The existing fix on `wl-SA-0MPKAZUWF0046EQJ-input-echo-detection` may need to be reviewed and either merged or replaced.
- **Assumption**: The Local Proxy endpoint at 192.168.0.199:8000 being down is the trigger for the false success path; when it's up, Local Proxy may work correctly but use the wrong model.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions were asked during this intake — the existing work item description and repository context were sufficient to draft this intake brief. The description was already exceptionally detailed with root cause analysis, reproduction steps, log evidence, and potential fix options.

## Intake Brief: Multi-agent audit/test coordination to break deadlocks

## Work item
**SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF -- When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing**

## Problem statement

When multiple agents run concurrently (herdr-dispatched implement/plan/audit panes plus manual sessions), audits and test runs contend for the same scarce host resources (local LLM slots, audit concurrency slots, CPU) and end up blocking one another. Two mechanisms interact to create a livelock/starvation pattern: (1) the herdr downtime worker only dispatches any work -- including audits -- after the local LLM has been **continuously idle >=60s with >=2 free slots**; (2) the audit runner **fails fast (0s wait)** when the host-wide audit semaphore is saturated, returning `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts. Under sustained agent traffic the idle gate never opens, so audits starve; in the rare dispatch windows, concurrent audits may still collide and fail-fast, keeping items `in_review` indefinitely. Tableau-Card-Engine currently shows 28 items in `in_review` -- several 1000+ hours old (up to 4178h) -- with only 15 audit dispatches ever recorded and one audit running 8+ hours. A coordination mechanism is needed so audits proceed with bounded, prioritized concurrency independent of a strict "all traffic quiet" gate.

## Users

- **Concurrent agent herd** (herdr instances + pi panes on the same machine) running implement/plan/audit sessions -- they block on audits of their completed items.
- **Audit skill consumers** -- every completed/item-in-`in_review` work item needs a timely audit verdict to progress/close.
- **Operator (rgardler)** -- watches the worklog; a deadlocked herd produces no visible progress and wasted LLM spend.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No fail-fast re-queue under load (north star):** under sustained concurrent agent/LLM traffic, audits no longer return `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts as the *common* outcome; when the ceiling is momentarily saturated, audits wait on a bounded queue (or equivalent) rather than failing immediately. Verification: run N >= 3 concurrent audits against a busy host; zero concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts; all audits persist real verdicts.
2. **Bounded audit turnaround (realistic start):** an `in_review` item is audited within N hours (N to be tuned) of entering that stage while multiple agents are active. Verification: seed/observe items entering `in_review` under concurrent load; 95th-percentile time-to-audit <= N. Note: turnaround is bounded within dispatch windows; the gate-opening frequency is the hard throughput ceiling (see AC3 amendment).
3. **Idle-gate decoupling for audits (amended):** *within any dispatch window*, audit dispatch/progress no longer requires a strict continuous LLM idle window; audits proceed under high agent traffic (bounded by the host-wide audit semaphore), while non-audit dispatch may retain a gentler gate. Note: the idle gate itself is unchanged (see SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 follow-up); this AC is satisfied by the bounded-queue mechanism ensuring audits proceed without fail-fast once a dispatch window opens.
4. **Priority ordering:** among queued/waiting audit candidates, `critical` items are audited before `high`, then age/FIFO; no item is bypassed indefinitely. Verification: deterministic ordering observed in logs/tests; the 4178h-old backlog drains.
5. **No regression to existing guards:** per-item `in_progress` claim guard, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight, lease/leader machinery, and test-cache read-only consumption all continue to work unchanged (see Constraints). **All related documentation updated** (audit skill reference, process_semaphore, AGENTS.md coordination section, downtime-dispatcher doc if touched). **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Single-machine scope (v1) matches herdr's current leader-election/lease model; no new network service.
- Preserve the cross-process flock semaphore primitive (no stale locks); extend semantics (bounded wait/priority/queueing) rather than replace wholesale.
- The dispatcher cannot know a work item's weight before dispatch -- fine-grained coordination belongs in the skills (audit/test) where concurrency is actually consumed; dispatcher changes should be minimal and only where they unblock (e.g., audits not gated on full idle).
- Must not destabilize working coordination machinery: leader lease (5-min TTL), 30-min check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups.
- Keep test execution cheap: the per-repo test cache (2h TTL) already dedupes suite runs; do not regress read-only cache consumption by audits/implement/ship.
- Respect `.gitignore`/agent-framework rules; changes to `skill/`, `command/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` are tracked here, built, tested, pushed to `dev` per the global workflow.

## Plan

### Feature breakdown (5 child items, 3 vertical slices)

**Slice 1 -- Zero fail-fast + priority ordering (AC1, AC4):**
- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (task) -- Implement shared bounded priority queue module in `skill/shared/queue.py`
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (feature) -- Integrate audit runner with bounded queue (replaces fail-fast) + queue logging

**Slice 2 -- Batch drain (AC2):**
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** (feature) -- Add batch drain mode (process N items per window)

**Slice 3 -- Broader scope + research (AC5):**
- **SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG** (task) -- Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive
- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** (task) -- Evaluate whether idle-gate relaxation is needed (research, independent)

### Dependency graph
```
SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L (queue module) -- foundation, no deps
  |-- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM (queue integration)
  |     |-- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (batch drain)
  |-- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill)
SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 (gate eval) -- independent research
```

### Sequencing with related work
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** (stale-audit detection, completed/in_review): same file area (`audit_runner.py`) but different path. This item modifies the concurrency/semaphore/launch path; SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC works on the freshness/fingerprint path. Implement SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC first to avoid overlapping edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` -- `_acquire_audit_slot()` (2124), `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (134-135, 0s default), saturation verdict path (2796-2855); central place to add bounded wait/queue.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` -- counting semaphore (already supports `timeout>0` bounded wait; may need priority/fairness or a queue protocol, plus tests at `skill/shared/tests/`).
- `skill/shared/queue.py` -- **new**: bounded priority queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` -- suite run/dedup layer; candidate for the same coordination primitive if test runs contend.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (ContextHub) -- idle gate/dispatch tiers; candidate for the audit-gate relaxation (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 research).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (ContextHub), `packages/herdr/README.md` (ContextHub), `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` coordination section -- docs to update.

## Related work

Potentially related work items (SorraAgents):
- SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC -- Eliminate wasteful re-audits: stale-audit detection and cross-session audit coordination (completed/in_review, **same file area** `audit_runner.py` -- distinct concern: front freshness fast-path vs. this item's contention/queueing; sequence to avoid overlapping edits)
- SA-0MSAK2SNN005HCM5 -- Audit runner concurrency cap (completed; the existing bound)
- SA-0MSAK2P3J0065POO -- Shared cross-process semaphore module (completed; primitive to extend)
- SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL -- Audit skill: fail immediately when audit concurrency limit is reached (completed; the behavior this item supersedes with bounded queueing)
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB -- Investigate audit concurrency TimeoutError errors (completed)
- SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 -- Investigate concurrent audit fan-out causing extreme load (completed; fan-out context for ceilings)
- SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY -- Cache full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement (completed)
- SA-0MSL1YS4K008HJVU -- Audit skill improvements: P1-P3 optimization backlog (open, plan_complete; watch for overlap)

ContextHub (WL-) related: downtime dispatcher leader election WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL, no-candidate cooldown WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX, coordination-mode WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7, critical-first dispatch WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE, idle-gate slot requirements WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should this item (a) produce an investigation+proposal that stops, (b) go straight to designing and implementing a coordination mechanism, or (c) be an epic decomposed into investigation->design->implementation children?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) -- go straight to designing and implementing." Source: interactive reply 2026-08-30. Implies single feature item (issueType set to `feature`), with plan stage free to decompose as needed.
- Q2: "Where should the mechanism live -- audit/test skills, herdr dispatcher, or both?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "Wherever makes the most sense -- note the dispatcher may be too late as it cannot know what the work items will entail ahead of dispatch -- happy if you have a good idea."
  - Research (Map): dispatcher-side gating cannot know item weight pre-dispatch; the contention is consumed skill-side (audit semaphore, subprocess launches). Primary surface: `skill/audit` bounded prioritized queue on the existing flock semaphore; dispatcher relaxation (secondary) only to stop the strict idle gate from starving audits. Accepted as design direction; refinement at plan stage.
- Q3: "What measurable success? (a) every in_review audited within N hours, (b) zero 'concurrency limit reached' unmet verdicts, or other?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) is the north star goal; (a) may be a realistic start -- your guidance is required once you have evaluated."
  - Guidance (Map): north-star AC1 = zero fail-fast `unmet` verdicts under load; start-gate AC2 = bounded turnaround (initial N=24h, tuned from observed dispatch/backlog data: 28 items stuck, ~1 valid audit window per couple hours). AC1 is achievable now with bounded-wait queueing (semaphore already supports `timeout>0`); AC2 additionally needs idle-gate decoupling (AC3) so dispatches aren't rare. Priority ordering (AC4) addresses the oldest-first fairness gap.

### Plan design decisions (2026-08-30)

- Q1 (Queue protocol): **(a) File-based priority queue** (RECOMMENDED). Answer (operator/rgardler): confirmed. A shared queue directory where each waiter writes a priority+timestamp file; dispatcher reads in order (critical>high>age).
- Q2 (Idle gate): **(b) Keep gate, rely on bounded wait**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "We cannot loosen the gate, which means b is the only option. What impact does this have on ACs? What can be done?" AC3 amended: "within any dispatch window, audits proceed without fail-fast"; AC2 amended: turnaround bounded within windows, gate-opening frequency is throughput ceiling. Batch drain mode (process multiple items per window) mitigates throughput impact.
- Q3 (Scope): **(b) Shared primitive, audit first consumer, test second**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "implementation runs audits, scoping to audit only will have limited effect." The shared primitive in `skill/shared/` is consumed by audit first; test skill extended in a separate task. A follow-up research item (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50) evaluates whether the idle gate should be relaxed.

## Recommendations & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bounded-wait + fairness ordering on the existing semaphore is sufficient for AC1; a formal FIFO/priority queue (file-based) for AC2/AC4 is the natural extension and the core of this feature.
- **Assumption:** audits are the scarce op (tests already cached); the feature centers on audit coordination, with test coordination as a separate task.
- **Assumption:** the strict idle gate exists to protect interactive use (reserve >=1 slot); relaxation is outside v1 scope (tracked as SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50).
- **Risk:** touching audit-runner concurrency paths regresses the many hardening fixes in that file (parent-timeout, stall detection, retry/backoff). Mitigation: surgical change in `_acquire_audit_slot`/verdict path only; run the full audit test suite.
- **Risk:** queue/prioritization adds state; a crash could strand waiting items. Mitigation: flock-based no-stale-lock design (kernel release), plus item-level retry markers so no item is lost.
- **Risk:** dispatcher-side change (if taken) interacts with herdr election/lease fail-closed logic. Mitigation: keep it minimal and documented; test tiers remain.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tuning N, backlog draining of all 28 TCE items, or building a general scheduler are separate concerns -- recorded as follow-up items if they arise, not scope here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-08-30 Plan skill (Map):** decomposed into 5 child items across 3 vertical slices. Design decisions: file-based priority queue (Q1a), bounded-wait replaces fail-fast with gate unchanged (Q2b), shared primitive scope includes test skill (Q3b). AC2/AC3 amended to reflect gate-stay constraint. Follow-up research item created for gate evaluation.

data.description:
# Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for child audits in the final-validation gate

## Problem statement

The ship skill's final-validation gate (Step 6) sweeps ALL `in_review` items — top-level and children — and blocks on any child whose audit is missing/stale/failing. This contradicts Steps 2 (audit readiness) and 5 (producer review), which are deliberately top-level scoped, and the documentation's own statement that "Child items are covered by their parent's audit and never block." The result is that a release can be blocked by child audit gaps that are either already covered by a passing parent audit or outside the release scope.

## Users

- **Release manager:** wants to ship without being blocked by child audit gaps that are already covered by the parent's audit or outside the release scope.
- **Ship skill automation:** needs deterministic rules for child-audit scoping so the release is repeatable without operator intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parent coverage:** the final-validation gate treats a child as `passing` (non-blocking) when its parent (resolved via `parentId`) has a **fresh passing** audit (`readyToClose === true`), and records the coverage in the gate report (e.g. "N child(ren) covered by passing parent audit <parentId>").
2. **Out-of-scope exclusion:** the final-validation gate **excludes** a child whose parent is not in stage `in_review` (i.e. the parent is not part of the release) — such children never block, and are reported as excluded with the parent id and stage.
3. **Conservative fallback:** parent coverage does **not** apply when the parent audit is missing, stale, transient, or failing. An uncovered child with a missing/stale/failing audit still blocks exactly as today (exit 12).
4. **Top-level behaviour unchanged:** top-level `in_review` items are evaluated exactly as today; the new rules apply only to children.
5. **Recursion/ancestors:** coverage resolves through the parent chain safely — a child of a child (grandchild) is covered by its nearest `in_review` ancestor with a passing audit; a non-`in_review` ancestor excludes the subtree.
6. **Hermetic unit tests** (injectable boundaries; no live `wl`/`audit_runner`): (a) covered child passes; (b) uncovered child with a failing audit still blocks; (c) child of a non-`in_review` parent is excluded; (d) parent with a stale audit does not cover; (e) grandchild resolves via nearest passing ancestor; (f) a child whose `parentId` references a deleted/non-existent item is handled per AC13 (no crash, deterministic outcome).
7. **Documentation:** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` describe the parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules and their precedence, so the decision is repeatable without operator intervention.
8. **Exit codes unchanged:** the gate still exits 12 on genuine uncovered failures; successful runs still exit 0.
9. **Scoped close:** the close-work-items step closes only items in the release candidate set (and, when recursing, only descendants that are themselves candidates or are explicitly included) — a `--force` recursive close must not close descendants outside the candidate set. An excluded subtree nested beneath a shipped item survives the release intact.
10. **Collateral detection/report:** the close step reports any descendant it would close outside the candidate set, and any such closure is either refused or recorded as an explicit, reversible exclusion decision.
11. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, SKILL.md, and the ship skill reference docs.
12. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
13. **Deleted/non-existent parent (orphan) handling:** when a child's `parentId` references a work item that does not exist (deleted), the gate must not crash and must behave deterministically: the orphan is NOT treated as covered (it has no passing parent to inherit from) and is either excluded from the release candidate set with the reason recorded, or evaluated on its own audit — consistent with the Precedence rules. Deleting a parent must not leave its children blocking indefinitely without an explicit, documented outcome.

## Precedence

For each child, evaluate in order:
1. Parent not in `in_review` → **excluded** (not part of the release).
2. Parent (nearest `in_review` ancestor) has a fresh passing audit → **covered/satisfied**.
3. Otherwise → evaluate the child's own audit (missing/stale/transient → auto-remediate; failing → block).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** parent-coverage resolution only applies to `in_review` parents; any further scoping rules (e.g. `completed` status, other stages) are recorded as linked work items, not added here.
- **Circular references:** a work item referencing itself or forming a parent cycle would cause infinite recursion; the implementation must detect and break cycles.
- **Performance:** resolving parent chains for many `in_review` items could be expensive; a bounded parent cache is noted in the implementation plan.
- **Close step regression:** scoping the close step may uncover other subtrees that were previously swept; these should be tested explicitly.

## Constraints

- Changes must not alter the exit-code contract (exit 12 for genuine failures, exit 0 for success).
- Parent-coverage resolution must be bounded (avoid infinite loops in circular references).
- The close-work-items step must not close items outside the candidate set, preserving work in progress on non-release workstreams.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` queries **all** `in_review` items (top-level + children) and blocks on any audit issue.
- Steps 2 and 5 are top-level scoped (`parentId == null`), creating the documented contradiction.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` close-work-items uses `wl close --force` which recursively closes descendants, including non-candidate subtrees.
- No existing unit tests for `check-final-validation.js`.

## Desired change

- Extend `check-final-validation.js` with parent-coverage + out-of-scope logic.
- Extend `run-release.js` close step with candidate-set scoping.
- Add hermetic unit tests.
- Update `SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — extend with parent-coverage + out-of-scope logic
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — scope close-work-items to candidate set
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — reuse `classifyAudit` / `isAuditStale`
- `skill/ship/tests/` — add unit tests (new file for check-final-validation tests)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document gate scoping rules

## Related work

- **SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ** – R4: Prevent concurrency saturation from aborting the Phase 1 parent screen (completed)
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MSGAUD3H007P8Y4** – P5: test _deep_analyze_child retry forwarding + timeout-default AC clarification (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions asked — the work item is sufficiently defined by the discovery context (TCE release 2026-09-15) and the operator's ruling recorded in the discovery comment.

## Appendix: v0.1.17 release findings (2026-09-23)

Observed during the `/skill:ship release` attempt that was blocked at Step 6 (final-validation gate, exit 12), after Steps 2 (audit readiness) and 5 (producer review) passed:

- **Scale:** the gate swept **104 `in_review` items**; **52** lacked a passing audit. Most were children whose parents had passed audit — exactly the case AC1/AC2 address.
- **Deleted parent (NEW edge case):** parent `SA-0MSRVN28E009OL5S` had been **deleted**, yet its **5 children** (`SA-0MSRVXECH0019962`, `SA-0MSRW9BV20029XEB`, `SA-0MSRW9FS0006CUYJ`, `SA-0MSRWB5LM0057VQ9`, `SA-0MSRWB1V7006IEW3`) remained `in_review` and blocked the gate. Deleting the parent did **not** stop its children from blocking. This is the case AC13 adds.
- **Transient infrastructure interaction:** one orphan (`SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB`) could not be re-audited (`Pi provider error: Connection error.`, ~713 s) due to a stale-ctx exception in the `proxy-compaction-bridge` extension — see SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F. It was manually deleted by the operator to proceed. This reinforces that a child blocked only by a transient/provider error must not hard-block the release.
- **Documentation contradiction confirmed:** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` Step 6 currently states the gate is "deliberately **not** top-level-scoped", which is the opposite of the operator's ruling that children are covered by a passing parent (AC1/AC2/AC7/AC11 must correct this text).
- **Operator ruling (2026-09-23):** "Step 6 should be top level only. As long as the parent passes audit then children are assumed to do so."

## Implementation

**check-final-validation.js** — added parent-coverage / out-of-scope resolution:
- `getItemById(id)` — resolves any item by id for parent-chain walks; returns `null` only for genuine not-found (deleted/missing), throws on command failure (treated conservatively as *uncovered*, never silently excluded).
- `resolveChildScope(item, boundaries)` — precedence: (1) deleted/missing parent → `excluded`; (2) non-`in_review` ancestor → `excluded`; (3) nearest `in_review` ancestor with a fresh passing audit → `covered`; (4) else `uncovered`. Non-passing `in_review` ancestors are skipped so a higher passing ancestor can cover; cycles break conservatively.
- `checkFinalValidation` now skips covered/excluded children (they never block, including producer flags), evaluates uncovered children + top-level items as before, and reports `coveredChildren`/`excludedChildren` grouped by parent. New `getItemByIdFn` injection boundary.

**run-release.js** — close-step candidate-set scoping (AC9/AC10):
- `getDescendants(itemId)` — recursive `wl show --children` walk (cycle-bounded).
- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` refuses (skips) any candidate whose `--force` close would sweep descendants outside the close-candidate set; reports `refusedItems`. New `getDescendantsFn` boundary.

**Tests:** 70 ship unit tests green (covered/excluded/orphan/stale-parent/grandchild/cycle + close refusal); full node unit suite 419/419; eslint clean.

**Docs:** SKILL.md and both ship-skill-reference docs updated with precedence rules, new exports, and close scoping.
